{{nihongo|'''Ikenimasu-asagirikihatahime Shrine'''|池坐朝霧黄幡比売神社}} is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945}} located in {{ill|Nara Prefecture|Q131287|qid=Q131287}}{{ill|Shiki District, Nara|Q1155036|qid=Q1155036}}{{ill|Tawaramoto, Nara|Q1203159|qid=Q1203159}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinai Taisha|ja|式内大社|simple|Shikinai Taisha|qid=Q134917288}}, and its former {{ill|Shakaku|Q10444029|qid=Q10444029}} was {{ill|Gō-sha|Q134917316|qid=Q134917316}}. {{nihongo|'''Ikenimasu-asagirikihatahime Shrine'''|池坐朝霧黄幡比売神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Yamato Province]].

== History ==
== Foundation ==
The exact date of foundation is unknown, but according to a stone monument standing within the precincts, “In the 24th year of {{ill|Empress Suiko|Q298057|qid=Q298057}} ({{ill|616|Q33263|qid=Q33263}}), the {{ill|Hata clan|Q987290|qid=Q987290}}, who were granted the temple compound of Hōkiji founded by {{ill|Prince Shōtoku|Q263972|qid=Q263972}}, revered this ancient shrine as the guardian deity of their ancestral god.” Based on this, it is inferred that the shrine was founded in the 24th year of Emperor Suiko by the Hata clan at the same time as the establishment of Hōkiji, and that it was venerated as the tutelary shrine of Hōkiji.

== Overview ==

it was known by the name “Tenman-gū.”

According to the *{{ill|Shiki District, Nara|Q1155036|qid=Q1155036}} Gazetteer*, “Hōkiji is an old temple said to have been founded by {{ill|Hata no Kawakatsu|Q5680877|qid=Q5680877}}, and is the clan temple of the {{ill|Hasegawa clan|Q11653880|qid=Q11653880|lt=Hasegawa faction}}. Therefore, another name for the Hasegawa faction is the people of Hōkiji. This shrine was likely invited as the tutelary deity of that temple compound. From ancient times, the temple managed its rites, and the Hasegawa faction’s involvement in them likely originates from this.” From this, it is said that Hōkiji was revered as the clan temple of the Hasegawa faction, and this shrine was likewise worshipped. Furthermore, in the *Meishukushū* written by {{ill|Konparu Zenchiku|Q1780792|qid=Q1780792}} of the {{ill|Konparu|Q4525036|qid=Q4525036}} of {{ill|Nōgaku|Q1037119|qid=Q1037119}}, who was the son-in-law of {{ill|Zeami Motokiyo|Q169352|qid=Q169352}}, it is written: “Of the three sons of Hata no Kawakatsu, one transmitted martial arts, one transmitted music, and one transmitted sarugaku. The descendants who transmitted martial arts are the present Hasegawa faction of Yamato.” From this, it is thought that the shrine also had close ties with the Hata clan.
